title: Hyperbolic Graph Neural Networks Under the Microscope: The Role of Geometry-Task Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2602.01828v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Many complex networks exhibit hierarchical, tree-like structures, making hyperbolic space a natural candidate wherein to learn representations of them. Based on this observation, Hyperbolic Graph Neural Networks (HGNNs) have been widely adopted as a principled choice for representation learning on tree-like graphs. In this work, we question this paradigm by proposing the additional condition of geometry--task alignment, i.e., whether the metric structure of the target follows that of the input graph. We start by empirically showing that HGNNs can recover low-distortion representations when supervision explicitly rewards metric preservation and proceed by theoretically analyzing a controlled regression setting in which a linear readout benefits from representations whose geometry is aligned with the target metric. Finally, by relying on both predictive performance and embedding distortion, we further show that HGNNs gain an advantage

translated_title: 显微镜下的双曲图神经网络：几何-任务对齐的作用
translated_abstract: 许多复杂网络呈现出层次化的树状结构，这使得双曲空间成为学习其表示的天然候选。基于这一观察，双曲图神经网络（HGNNs）已被广泛采用作为树状图表示学习的一种有原则的选择。在这项工作中，我们通过提出几何-任务对齐这一额外条件来质疑这一范式，即目标的度量结构是否遵循输入图的度量结构。我们首先通过实验证明，当监督信号明确奖励度量保持时，HGNNs 能够恢复低失真的表示；随后我们从理论上分析了一个受控回归设置，其中线性读出层受益于几何与目标度量对齐的表示。最后，通过结合预测性能和嵌入失真两个方面，我们进一步表明 HGNNs 在（几何-任务对齐的条件下）获得优势。
tldr: 这项工作提出“几何-任务对齐”这一关键条件，通过实验和理论分析表明，双曲图神经网络只有在任务的度量结构与输入图的几何结构相匹配时才能真正获得优势。
en_tdlr: This work introduces the condition of geometry-task alignment, demonstrating through empirical and theoretical analysis that Hyperbolic Graph Neural Networks only gain an advantage when the target's metric structure matches the geometry of the input graph.
